page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-16-lssd is a general-purpose compute instance based on the x86_64 architecture. The server features 16 dedicated virtual CPU cores paired with 62 GB of total system memory, providing an average of 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned on this instance type.

The configuration includes 403 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The integrated solid-state disk delivers direct host-attached storage access for workloads requiring high local read and write operations without exclusive dependency on network-attached volumes. In terms of external networking provisions, the instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

With its 1:4 CPU-to-memory distribution and dedicated core allocation, the hardware footprint is balanced between general computation and low-latency storage throughput. This setup fits transactional databases, distributed CI/CD build environments, web application backends, and data processing tasks requiring high-speed temporary storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-16-lssd is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs, 62 GB of system memory, and a bundled 403 GB local NVMe solid-state drive. It maintains a balanced resource profile of approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per virtual CPU core, operating without discrete GPU acceleration. The inclusion of host-level NVMe storage provides localized, low-latency disk capability without relying solely on network volumes, favoring I/O-sensitive application caching. Dedicated allocation ensures steady processing across all 16 cores, while complimentary public IPv4 addressing is omitted by default. This balance of dedicated compute, mid-tier memory capacity, and direct-attached storage makes the instance appropriate for transactional database hosting, container workloads, data processing pipelines, and build systems requiring local scratch space.
